neighbours.label: Weak guess: the slot before making someone do something, promoting 'make' (you can't [make] him eat, and get him to); ordinary verbs stay quiet
fire: You can bring a horse to a stream, but you can't make it drink.
You can offer kids broccoli, but you can't make them like it.
How do I talk my son out of bed and get him to walk the dog?
You can send them to class, but you can't force them to learn.
We can give him the map, but we can't make him read it.
How do I lift my daughter from the sofa and get her to study?
You can pay a man to sit, but you can't make him care.
They can buy the seeds, but they can't make them grow.
quiet: You can bring a horse to a stream and let it rest.
You can offer kids broccoli with a little cheese on top.
How do I get to the station from the old bridge by bus?
You can send them a card for her birthday in May.
We can give him the map at the door on Friday.
How do I sign up for the morning class at the gym?
You can pay at the desk or use the machine.
They can buy the seeds at the shop near the bank.

notes: The output direction promotes make, makes, making (on this pole). Probes: 0.79 and 0.29, others under 0.15. Japanese causatives on the card read 0.01.
